title: Cheap to Copy
goal: A two-int point crosses this code four times. Pick the version that never allocates OR clones.
hints: Two i32s are 8 bytes — smaller than the pointer you'd pass them by.
derive(Copy) makes passing a Point behave like passing an int: duplicate, don't move.
explanation: A struct of two i32s is exactly the kind of type Copy exists for: deriving Copy makes every pass-by-value a bit-for-bit duplicate, so the moves that forced cloning simply stop being moves. All three versions pass the tests; the Copy version deletes every clone() by changing one derive. The instinct: small, plain-data structs (no heap fields) should derive Copy, and clone() on them is a smell.
